condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: All L1 gold contexts report oral bioavailability at or above 20%; the lowest values are PLP 23.7% and acalabrutinib 25%, and no L1 context affirmatively supports F < 20%.

L2 absolute measurements reinforce the same direction: amrinone 93 ± 12%, tolfenamic acid about 100–126%, PAS uncoated capsules 118 ± 41%, acalabrutinib in dogs 54–75%, PF-592379 in rats 28% and dogs 61–87%, and GaM in dogs 40%.

The only sub-20% L2 values are relative formulation comparisons (enteric-coated PAS 0% relative to solution) and do not define the accepted gold outcome; they are formulation-specific and not transferable to the query.

The query is a low-molecular-weight p-aminobenzenesulfonamide isoxazole; the closest supplied contexts (PABA, PAS, selurampanel) all show high F, and the mixed physicochemical prior is not affirmative evidence of low F.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule is available in the supplied records.
No context exactly matches the p-aminobenzenesulfonamide-isoxazole scaffold; transfer is analogical.
Formulation effects are unknown; PAS enteric-coated tablets had 0% relative bioavailability (C64, C70), so formulation could be a modifier.
Low neutral fraction (0.06) and high TPSA (98.22) may limit passive absorption, but no query-specific absorption or first-pass data are available.
Species differences (e.g., PF-592379 rat 28% vs dog 61–87%) add uncertainty in extrapolation.
